# dsh-token-usage
> Token usage analytics and a model capability leaderboard — a DeepSeek Harness plugin.

It scans **the host's own session logs**, groups the records by provider and model,
and reports cons

umption trends, cache hit rates and per-model usage. It then lines
up **every model you can currentl

y call** against a public capability leaderboard,
so you can see which of them is the strongest.
| Capability | Entry point |
| Usage panel | Sidebar "Token usage" → main panel (summary figures + four charts + a detail table)

|
| Usage JSON | `GET {prefix}/usage` (supports `days=` and `refresh=1`) |
| Model leaderboard | Bot

tom of the usage panel (overall ranking + six task recommendations) |
| Leaderboard JSON | `GET {pre
fix}/model-rank` (supports `refresh=1`) |

**This plugin never touches your accounts.** It only reads the host's own session
logs: no OAuth flo

w, no credential copying, no model provider registration, no
changes to any client.
## How it relates to `dsh-agent-checkin`
**It doesn't.** The two plugins are fully independent and can be installed alone:
| | `dsh-agent-checkin` | `dsh-token-usage` |
| What it does | Daily check-ins, credit balances, wiring local clients up as model providers | Toke

n usage analytics, model capability leaderboard |
| Data source | The sign-in state of local clients

| The host's own session logs |
| Reads the other one's files? | —— | **No** |

The usage panel used to live inside `dsh-agent-checkin` (0.8.0 and earlier). As of
0.9.0 it is a sep

arate plugin: they share no code, no cache files, and never call
each other. Installing one has no e

.0`

when `DSH_HOME` is unset)

## Usage
### The usage panel
Click "Token usage" in the sidebar. From top to bottom the panel shows:

1. **Summary figures** — total consumption / today / last 7 days / call count, plus
cache hits, cach

e misses and the hit rate
2. **Four charts** — consumption trend (bars; the time window — 7 / 30 / 9

0 days or
"all" — lives in this card's corner and affects only this chart, alongside the
daily / cum

ulative toggle), by-provider breakdown (donut), top models by usage,
and a capability ranking of the

models you actually used
3. **Source detail table** — per provider/model input, cache reads and wri

tes,
output, total, call count, hit rate, tokens per call and output share
4. **Model leaderboard**

— an overall ranking (every scored model included; a model
callable through several platforms is mer

ged into one row with all platforms listed
in the source column and the stats line noting "merged in

to N models"; 10 rows
shown by default, scroll inside the table for the rest, row count in the corne

r)
plus recommendations by task (coding / research / writing / slides /
data work / cheapest), every

rankable model per task, scroll inside
the card
5. **Footer** — how many session files were scanned

, how long it took, and whether
the scan completed

The time window selector sits in the trend card's corner and only affects the trend
chart — summary

figures, the donut, rankings and the detail table always cover the
full history. "Refresh" forces a
re-scan; everything else uses the cache.
### How the numbers are computed
| Metric | Definition |
| Tokens per record | `inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens`, summed sepa

rately per segment |
| Hit rate denominator | `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite` (**excluding output**

— output is generated, not fed in) |
| Zero denominator | Shows "—", **not 0%** ("couldn't read it"

and "really zero" are different things) |
| Day boundary | Local time zone, not UTC |
| "Total" | A
ll history; the three cache figures use the same baseline, so the numbers reconcile |

> **Why not the `totalTokens` field**: it is an older measure and is not guaranteed
> to match the s

um of the four segments. Every total on the page is summed from the
> four segments.
>
> **Why only

`assistant/message`**: `assistant/attempt` carries a copy of the same
> usage record; counting both
would double the total for no reason.
### The incremental cache

Session logs only ever grow, so there is no reason to rescan everything each time.
The scanner recor

ds each file's `size + mtime` and only re-reads the files that
changed, reusing the previous row-lev
el aggregation for the rest.

- Cold full scan: a few dozen logs / tens of MB, about 1.4 seconds
- Routine refresh: single-digit m

illiseconds once the cache is warm
- No SQLite: no native dependency, no schema migration, no half-w

once the cache is warm
- No SQLite: no native dependency, no schema migration, no half-written state
### The model leaderboard
The ranking draws on two sources, kept **strictly separate**:

- **Capability scores** — a public leaderboard (OpenRouter's `/api/v1/models`, no
auth required, car

rying Artificial Analysis's intelligence / coding / agentic
indices plus context length, price and i

nput modalities)
- **Scope** — **every model callable through this host right now**: the official
`c

tx.llm` (LlmRuntime) enumerates each registered provider's advertised models,
so every enable/disabl
e you make in "Platforms & Models" is reflected faithfully
So the board answers "of the models I can call, which one fits which task best".

> answers "what is
